title: hollow-is-measured-a-proof-must-red-when-its-build-is-reverted
author: CC
cast_under: Akien 2026-09-07: 'the 19 at proveme. what's the really, really right way to do this? spare no expense kind of thing?' -> CC's three pieces of physics -> 'then lets do that.'
intention: Hollow is measured, not asserted: a tester verb reverts each file a ticket's build wrote to its pre-build version in a scratch worktree, runs the named proof there, and requires at least one tooth declared for that ticket to go red per file -- recording the result on the seal.
why: Law 8 says a proof a hollow build couldn't pass, and today that clause is read, never run: measured 2026-09-07, 'hollow' appears in the tester once, in a comment (cli.py:82), and in no seal record. The four false greens found the same day (three tickets on test_trouble_panel.py, one on test_codemother.py) passed every check the system has because every check asks 'did the proof pass?' and none asks 'would it have passed without the build?'. The lived symptom: a peer leans on a green that proves nothing, and finds out in production -- exactly the 'hollow green worse than a red' Law 8 names.
how: (a) `cairn test --hollow <ticket-id>`: read the ticket; resolve its decompose berth (chart_chain.decompose) and collect every sub_problem's writes_to under the cairn repo; read the BUILDME crossing's `at` from the ticket's owning journal (crossings carry at, proven_by, fingerprint; no commit) and take the pre-build commit as `git rev-list -1 --before=<at> HEAD`. (b) Create one scratch git worktree per run under the tester's scratch root (scratch.py), and for each writes_to file: check out the pre-build version there (`git show <commit>:<path>`), or remove it when it did not exist then; run the named proof in that worktree through run_proof (cwd = worktree, PYTHONPATH = worktree) with the instance swap the tester already uses; read evidence.teeth_green against PROVES[ticket] (tool cairn/tools/proof_coverage, ticket proof-coverage-is-declared-...); restore the file before the next. A file whose reversion reds no declared tooth is named: 'hollow: <file> reverted, no declared tooth redded' and the verb exits non-zero. (c) The result lands as evidence.hollow[ticket] = {file: [teeth that redded]} on the proof's seal record through persist_validation -- inside evidence, no ninth field; `--seal --hollow <ticket>` seals and measures in one run so the record is one write. (d) The worktree is removed at exit and on failure; the live tree is never touched (git status before == after, a tooth in the proof). The PROVEME->PROVED gate (ticket 1accdc1781aa) REQUIRES evidence.hollow[ticket] on the seal with no hollow file named, for every code-seam; absent evidence is a deterministic red exactly as an absent seal is (ruling 2026-08-10 clearance-is-mandatory; Akien 2026-09-07: 'Gates are supposed to be hard, deterministic, state changes'). There is no advisory mode. Depends on P1 (PROVES + teeth_green).
falsifier: DONE when: (1) a fixture ticket whose decompose berth lists one writes_to file and whose proof declares one tooth for it: with the file reverted the declared tooth reds and the verb reports {file: [tooth]}, exit 0; (2) a fixture whose proof stays green after the reversion is reported 'hollow: <file> reverted, no declared tooth redded', exit non-zero; (3) the live working tree is byte-identical before and after a run -- git status and a content hash of the writes_to files, measured in the proof; (4) the result lands as evidence.hollow[ticket] on the seal record and the record still carries exactly the ratified eight fields; (5) run against 9579a6f9cec6 once built, every writes_to file reds at least one declared tooth, recorded in that ticket's PROVEME crossing. WRONG INTENT if a full run on one ticket exceeds 5 minutes wall-clock on this box: then the per-file loop shares one worktree and one instance swap, not a different design.
traces_to: Law 8 -- verbatim: 'a proof a hollow build couldn't pass'; this is that clause as a verb. Law 3 -- nothing is known until measured; 'the proof exercises the build' was a hypothesis on every seal to date. Law 4 -- the rule becomes physics on the seal record. Law 9 -- a hollow green is worse than a red because a peer leans on it (Law 8's why: trust).
owner: tester (cairn/devices/tester) owns the verb, the worktree and the evidence; CC builds
watchme: none, because evidence.hollow rides the seal record beside every proof (cairn/devices/tester/validation_store.py persist_validation) and the inspector's component_color already reads seal records -- the count of seals carrying hollow evidence is a grep over cairn/**/validations/*.json
children: none, because the verb, the worktree and the evidence write are one seam under one owner; the declaration it reads is cast separately (proof-coverage-is-declared-...)

crossings.note: Akien 2026-09-07: 'then lets do that. the box wants a restart for updates so we get everything ready, come back up into opus and build build build.' Chart chain orient..validate berthed 2026-09-07; cast + charted + crossed in one act by Fable for Opus to build.

`cairn test --hollow <ticket>` built across three pieces (scratch.scratch_worktree, hollow.py + the verb, validation_store.record_hollow). 10 teeth green 4 runs back to back, 0 worktree registrations left behind. FOUR states not two: covered, hollow, `unreadable` (the proof died on import — every tooth reds, which would otherwise read as perfect coverage) and `unwritten` (the revert changed nothing — a finding against the chart's writes_to). A run in which every file was skipped is a RED. Fixed in flight under ruling 2026-09-09-a-bug-the-voyage-uncovers-is-fixed-by-that-voyage: same-size same-second rewrites reused stale __pycache__, so the verb read a tree that did not exist and credited the wrong file for a red — 3 wrong answers in 14 runs.

amended.why_verbatim: Akien: Gates are supposed to be hard, deterministic, state changes. no hollow evidence. that sounds like a bug.
amended.what: how: the 'nope makes it advisory' switch on the PROVEME->PROVED gate is removed; the gate requires evidence.hollow, deterministically

PROVED. The verb works, and the defect it carried was not failure — it was SUCCEEDING WRONGLY. Two causes, one that mattered. git exports GIT_INDEX_FILE=.git/index (RELATIVE) and GIT_PREFIX= into every hook; the pre-commit hook runs the reseal door, which runs proofs as subprocesses that inherit them. scratch_worktree died loudly under that env in 0.12s — honest, fixed first, not the problem. hollow._restore, a `git -C <worktree> checkout -- <rel>`, resolved against the CALLER's index, did nothing and said nothing. So file N stayed reverted while N+1 was measured, N+1's teeth redded for a reason unrelated to N+1, that red read as 'a declared tooth checks this file', and A FILE THAT REALLY WAS HOLLOW WAS REPORTED ok. A hollow read as green, manufactured inside the catcher built to find one — Law 8's false green, leaned on by a peer. `git -C <root>` is no defence anywhere: GIT_DIR and its siblings outrank it everywhere.

THE FIX, AND THE PART THAT GENERALISES. _git_env became public git_env(); every tester git call meaning 'the repository I am pointing at' now takes it (3 in scratch.py, 4 in hollow.py, the fixtures in test_hollow.py). And _restore RAISES HollowUnmeasurable when the checkout fails — because the next thing to stop a checkout will not be an env var, and the verb must not measure past it (Law 3: a measurement that could not be taken may not travel home through the same return as a clean one). A 13th tooth pins that raise and is deliberately NOT coupled to the env var that revealed it — it fails the checkout by pointing at a directory that is no repository. Mutation-verified both ways. THE LINE NOT OVER-APPLIED, in the docstring because it is easy to get wrong: reseal.staged_files must NOT scrub — under `git commit -a` git writes a TEMPORARY index and points GIT_INDEX_FILE at it, so the hook's staged set lives there and nowhere else; scrubbing would read the pre-`-a` index and reseal the wrong proofs.

MEASURED. test_hollow.py under GIT_INDEX_FILE=.git/index GIT_PREFIX= went 4 failed -> 12 passed in 311.64s; seals 13 teeth_green / 0 teeth_red. Live fire `cairn test --seal --hollow 9579a6f9cec6` at HEAD 3159682: 8 measured, 0 hollow, 2 skipped, exit 0, 'SEALED — hollow evidence landed on 3 of 3 standing validation(s)', wall clock 2m7s against this ticket's 5-minute WRONG INTENT threshold — so the shared-worktree redesign that clause calls for is NOT owed. All three seals carry the eight ratified fields and evidence.hollow['9579a6f9cec6'] over 8 files.

OWED AND DELIBERATELY OUT OF BOUNDS, with the reason. 12 proof files and 11 non-proof modules shell `git -C <root>` and only 2 scrub: test_inspector.py, test_history_integrity.py and test_forwarding_derivation.py bare-inherit; test_ruling.py inherits os.environ straight into git. Not fixed here for a structural reason, not a tired one — git_env lives in cairn.devices.tester.scratch, so build_inspector's and ruling's proofs cannot import it without a cross-device import (ruled: only db_domain). Its right home is a tool, and picking that rung is design work rather than a patch. Owed to Akien, not silently dropped.
